questions.question: Which term does the two-magnon (second-order) striction vertex come from?

options.b: the bond-length derivative of J inserted into the BILINEAR (two-magnon) spin-wave Hamiltonian

questions.explanation: H3 = (b + b†) Ψ† M Ψ: one phonon operator times two magnon operators.

questions.question: Hands-on: FM chain with isotropic striction dJ/dr = 3 meV/Å. Linear magnon–phonon hybridisation?
questions.explanation: The linear vertex ∝ x_a·v_b vanishes for collinear order; the two-magnon vertex does not.

questions.question: Hands-on: FWHM (meV) of the longitudinal phonon at q = 0.9 Å⁻¹ in that FM chain at 300 K (3 decimals)?
questions.explanation: ≈ 0.144 meV from scattering of thermal magnons (k → k+q).

questions.question: Hands-on: how does that phonon width behave at low temperature (10 K)?

options.b: it vanishes (≈ 5×10⁻⁴ meV): no thermal magnons to scatter

questions.explanation: The scattering channel ∝ n(ε_k) − n(ε_k+q) dies out as the magnon population freezes.

questions.question: How was the vertex M(k, q) validated?

options.b: entry by entry against the first-order change of a frozen-phonon supercell Hamiltonian built by the independent LSWT code

questions.explanation: All blocks (scattering, pair creation, pair annihilation) agree to ~10⁻¹¹ for an AFM with anisotropy and complex patterns.

questions.question: A bug found that way was …

options.b: double counting of the pair terms (a real-space c3 a†a† term must be represented once)

questions.explanation: Comparing with the supercell showed the pair amplitude was twice too large until the duplicate assignment was removed.

questions.question: Why can the BZ sum of the 1D linewidth be checked semi-analytically?

options.b: in 1D the energy δ-function has explicit roots k*, giving γ = a Σ|S|²Δn/|∂(ε_k+q − ε_k)/∂k|

questions.explanation: Gaussian-smeared BZ sum and root formula agree to 10⁻⁵ relative.

questions.question: Hands-on: magnon at X of the FM chain at T = 0 — FWHM in meV (2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: ≈ 0.24 meV: spontaneous phonon emission (factor 1 + N + n) survives at T = 0.

questions.question: Which magnons can decay by emitting a phonon?

options.b: those for which ε(k) − ε(k−q) = ω(q) has solutions — typically magnons above the phonon band edge region

questions.explanation: Energy and momentum conservation restrict the channel; in the FM chain the width grows sharply above the phonon band.

questions.question: Hands-on: which phonon channel survives at T = 0 in the AFM chain?

options.b: decay into two magnons (pair creation from Bogoliubov pairing)

questions.explanation: (1 + n1 + n2) → 1 at T = 0: spontaneous two-magnon decay of optical phonons above 2× the magnon gap.

questions.question: Hands-on: magnon gap (meV) of the AFM chain at Γ (3 decimals)?
questions.explanation: ω = 2S√(K(2J+K)) type gap ≈ 3.317 meV for J = 4, K = 0.15, S = 1.5.

questions.question: Gilbert damping of a ferromagnetic magnon in the exact linearised LLG gives …
questions.explanation: Checked to 10⁻⁹ in the tests.

questions.question: Hands-on: AFM chain, α = 10⁻³: Gilbert FWHM of the Γ magnon in meV (4 decimals)?
questions.explanation: 0.0249 meV = 2α(2J + 2K)S — exchange-enhanced.

questions.question: Compared with 2αω at the AFM magnon gap (≈ 0.0066 meV), the AFM Gilbert width is …

options.b: ≈ 3.8 times larger and almost k-independent (exchange enhancement)

questions.explanation: Elliptical precession in an AFM dissipates through the exchange field.

questions.question: How was the AFM Gilbert result checked independently?

options.b: against the energy-dissipation formula γ = 2αω² Σ(|X|²+|Y|²)/ξ†𝓗ξ of the undamped modes

questions.explanation: Exact LLG eigenvalues and first-order dissipation agree to 10⁻³ relative at α = 10⁻³.

questions.question: Lattice friction η = 0.3 meV in the equation Ṗ = −∂H/∂u − ηP: FWHM of a pure phonon in meV?
questions.explanation: The amplitude decays at η/2, so the FWHM equals η.

questions.question: Which quantity in the golden rule of phonon decay into two magnons accounts for stimulated emission?
questions.explanation: (1+n1)(1+n2) − n1 n2 = 1 + n1 + n2 (forward minus reverse process).

questions.question: Phonon absorption by a magnon k → k+q enters the magnon linewidth with the factor …
questions.explanation: N(1 + n') − (1 + N) n' = N − n' for absorption; emission has 1 + N + n'.

questions.question: Which CLI options switch on the damping analysis in symphase magnons?
questions.explanation: They write *_linewidths.png/.dat with ω ± γ/2 for phonons and magnons.

questions.question: Why is the two-magnon process important for experiments on collinear magnets?

options.b: it gives temperature-dependent phonon and magnon linewidths (Raman, inelastic neutron/X-ray) even when linear magnon-polaron gaps vanish

questions.explanation: Spin–phonon damping appears as T-dependent broadening tied to the magnon population.
